Allenes in InChI

An allene has no stereocentre, yet it can be chiral. This page shows how InChI reads the handedness of the C=C=C axis from a drawing, and what is new: one wedge is enough, and the axis takes or and & labels.

1-Bromo-1-fluoro-3-chlorobuta-1,2-diene, drawn four ways. Strings from /t on:

Standard InChINew InChI
two wedges/t2-/m0/s1/t2-/m0/s1
one wedgeno stereo/t2-/m1/s1
or1/t2-/m0/s1/t2-/s2
&1/t2-/m0/s1/t2-/s3

With two wedges nothing changes. One wedge and the labels are new.

What makes an allene chiral

In C=C=C the two π bonds are perpendicular, so the substituents at one end lie in a plane at 90° to those at the other end. If each end carries two different groups, the molecule and its mirror image do not superimpose: the chirality sits on the axis, not on an atom. Chemists call the two forms Ra/Sa (or M/P).

InChI has no special layer for this. It writes the axis as if the central carbon were a stereocentre, in /t, with /m for the mirror image. So all the rules for stereocentres apply, including the enhanced labels:

1

abs or no label

The sample is the drawn enantiomer.

2

or1, or2, …

One enantiomer, unknown which.

or
3

&1, &2, …

Both enantiomers, 1:1.

+

The label goes on the central carbon of the allene.

From drawing to InChI, step by step

Example: the allene above, both ends wedged.

  1. You draw the allene with wedges

    A wedge at an end carbon shows which substituent points toward you. The other substituent at that end lies in the paper or behind it.

  2. InChI checks both ends

    • The chain is C=C=C (two cumulated double bonds).
    • Each end has two different substituents: here Br/F and CH₃/Cl.

    If an end has two equal groups there is no axis. Longer chains: see what InChI ignores.

  3. InChI reads the handedness from the wedges

    Two wedges, one at each end, define the axis. New: one wedge is enough. The flat end is taken to lie in the paper, the wedged end perpendicular to it, as IUPAC allows. Only under -EnhancedStereochemistry; standard InChI is unchanged.

    No wedge, or two wedges contradicting each other at one end: the axis is undefined and left out.

  4. InChI numbers the atoms

    Canonical numbers in grey. The central carbon is 2: the axis is written as stereo atom 2.

  5. InChI writes sign and mirror image

    As for a stereocentre, the axis gets a sign, + or −. A lone stereo element is always written -; /m records whether the drawing had to be mirrored for that.

    drawingInChImeaning
    as drawn/t2-/m0/s1no mirroring needed
    both wedges reversed/t2-/m1/s1mirrored: the other enantiomer

    /m0 and /m1 tell the two enantiomers apart; they do not map to Ra/Sa directly.

  6. A label on the central carbon sets the class

    With &1 on the central carbon, both mirror images are in the sample, so /m is dropped and /s3 says "racemic":

    /t2-/s3

    Both drawings, as drawn or reversed, give this string.

  7. The result

    InChI=1B/C4H3BrClF/c1-3(6)2-4(5)7/h1H3/t2-/m0/s1
    /t2-
    the axis, written on central carbon 2
    /m0
    which enantiomer (only when the axis is known absolutely)
    /s1
    class: absolute. /s2 = or, /s3 = &

    The prefix InChI=1B marks the string as enhanced.

Rules at a glance

Axis on the central carbon

An allene axis is one /t entry on its central carbon.

/t2-

Both ends must differ

Each end needs two different substituents, or there is no axis.

One wedge is enough

New, with -EnhancedStereochemistry. Standard InChI usually needs two.

Absolute axis = standard InChI

With no label or abs, only the prefix differs from standard InChI.

/t2-/m0/s1

Labels go on the central carbon

or gives /s2, & gives /s3, without /m. A label on an end carbon is ignored.

/t2-/s3

Mixed with stereocentres

The axis is grouped like any stereocentre: lowest member of each group reads −, groups listed by class.

/m0/s1(5)3(2)

Undefined axis is left out

No wedge, or contradicting wedges: nothing is written for the axis.

Allenes only

C=C=C only. C=C=C=C=C (four double bonds) is axial too but not supported yet; C=C=C=C (three) is E/Z.

What InChI ignores or leaves out

1Both ends flat

No wedge: the handedness is not drawn. The axis is left out.

InChI warns: Omitted undefined stereo
New InChI
no stereo
Standard InChI
no stereo
2Two wedges at one end

Both substituents of the same end point up: the drawing contradicts itself. Left out.

InChI warns: Omitted undefined stereo
New InChI
no stereo
Standard InChI
no stereo
3Label on an end carbon

&1 names an end carbon, not the central one. The label is ignored; the wedges count as absolute.

New InChI
/t2-/m0/s1
Standard InChI
/t2-/m0/s1
4Symmetric end

One end carries two methyls. The molecule equals its mirror image: no axis.

New InChI
no stereo
Standard InChI
no stereo
5Three double bonds (butatriene)

An even number of cumulated carbons: the ends are coplanar. This is E/Z, written in /b.

New InChI
/b4-3+
Standard InChI
/b4-3+
6Four double bonds (pentatetraene)

Axially chiral like an allene, but longer than InChI supports. No stereo is written.

New InChI
no stereo
Standard InChI
no stereo

Every InChI on this page is computed by the prototype (branch atropisomers, option -EnhancedStereochemistry), not typed in. Full rules: specification Allenes. More examples, old vs. new: comparison table.
